title: Mahavir, the brave little prince.
lines: Long ago, in India, in a city with beautiful palaces, a little prince was born.
His name was Vardhaman.
His daddy was the king and his mummy was the queen.
When Vardhaman was born, all sorts of lovely things happened.
The flowers opened, the trees grew fruit and everyone in the city was happy.
Vardhaman grew up and he was a very kind little boy.
He was friendly to everyone.
To people, to animals, and even to the smallest ant on the ground.
When he walked, he looked carefully where he put his feet, so he wouldn't hurt a single little creature.
One day Vardhaman was playing with his friends in the palace garden.
They were playing tag around a big tree.
Hee hee, you're it!
But suddenly the friends stopped.
They went pale.
Look!
shouted a boy.
A snake!
Around the big tree a big, fat snake was coiling.
Ssssss, hissed the snake.
It stuck out its tongue.
All the friends ran away and hid behind the bushes.
Help!
But Vardhaman stayed where he was.
He wasn't afraid.
He looked at the snake calmly.
He thought: this snake is just an animal too.
Maybe it's scared itself of all those children shouting and running.
Very slowly and very calmly Vardhaman walked up to the snake.
He spoke softly: Hello, snake.
Don't be afraid.
I won't hurt you.
And do you know what happened?
The snake calmed down.
It stopped hissing.
Vardhaman picked it up very carefully and carried it far away, to the forest, where the snake could live safely.
Bye, snake!
The friends came out from behind the bushes.
Wow, Vardhaman, you're so brave!
they said.
You're a real hero!
And from that day on people called him Mahavir.
Mahavir means: the great hero.
But Mahavir said: Being truly brave isn't fighting.
Being truly brave is staying calm and being kind to everything that lives.
When Mahavir grew up, he went all around the world to teach people that.
Don't hurt people, and don't hurt animals either.
Always tell the truth.
And share what you have with others.
And still today, when people see an ant on the ground and carefully step over it, they think of the kind prince Mahavir.
